claims.text: Section 8009, DoD Appropriations Act 2026: 'Funds appropriated by this Act may not be used to initiate, or materially modify the scope of, a special access program without prior notification 30 calendar days in advance to the congressional defense committees.'

Section 8009 binds only funds appropriated by that Act, so it does not reach an activity financed through contractor independent research and development reimbursement, through unvouchered CIA funds under 50 U.S.C. 3510, or through prior-year balances. Reasoning: the prohibition is drafted as a limitation on the use of that Act's appropriations, not as a general prohibition on unnotified SAPs.

connections.note: Section 8009 binds only funds appropriated by the annual Defense Appropriations Act; unvouchered Agency spending under 50 U.S.C. 3510 is neither DoD appropriated funds nor subject to normal expenditure law. desc: Section 8009 of the Department of Defense Appropriations Act for fiscal year 2026 provides, in a single sentence: 'Funds appropriated by this Act may not be used to initiate, or materially modify the scope of, a special access program without prior notification 30 calendar days in advance to the congressional defense committees.' It is the appropriations-side companion to the authorisation-side reporting regime of 10 U.S.C. 119, and it is a purer instrument, because it attaches to the money rather than to a reporting duty and because it contains no waiver. A programme initiated with funds appropriated by that Act without the 30-day notice is a programme operating on funds the statute says may not be used for it. This is the provision against which any concealed UAP-related special access programme would have to be measured, and it is also the provision that a programme predating 1988 - or funded from sources other than annual DoD appropriations, such as contractor IR&D reimbursement or the CIA's unvouchered account under 50 U.S.C. 3510 - would not touch at all.
label: Section 8009 - 30-day advance notice before initiating or materially modifying a special access program
